scenario: AITA for calling out professor for making fun of me in class? | Backstory real quick: (20M) I’m a ginger (orange hair, freckles, and I wear glasses as well) and have been made fun of for it for basically my whole life; I’ve had to hear just about every term in the book from firehead, red, carrot top, firecrotch, etc. All of it really pisses me off but I try to keep it to myself b/c god forbid people think I “can’t take a joke”. On several different occasions a professor I had in one of my tech classes this past semester made “jokes” about it. Second week of the year he says after forgetting my name “I’ll remember you, you’re the guy with no soul” and third week “Oh that’s right EverywhereForever, you’re the ginger with no soul”. Most of the class laughed, I was pissed and too embarrassed to say anything. It stopped for awhile after that though. Towards the end of the semester though he did it again, and I straight lost my cool and said “It’s not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day I walked in?” He didn’t say anything, class was quiet and he just continued with his lesson. I left for the bathroom b/c I was embarrassed and just got it together and walked back into class like nothing happened. The next day a kid talks to me outside class and said I was a dick about it and I just shrugged. Far be it from me to think something as arbitrary as my fucking hair color would be beyond juvenile and insulting remarks in college. AITA for the way I had reacted to this? This was mostly younger kids who had just graduated last year I think so I guess it may have influence on how they think but I wouldn’t expect it from a professor.

The user has a history of being teased for this, so it's a sensitive issue. The professor's comments are derogatory and could be considered harassment or bullying, especially since it's a power dynamic (professor-student). Even if the professor intended it as a joke, it's not okay to target someone's physical traits repeatedly.

When the user confronted the professor by saying "It's not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day?" that's a direct response to the behavior. He's pointing out the inappropriateness of the jokes. The question is whether this confrontation was morally acceptable.

In terms of moral acceptability, standing up against bullying or harassment is generally considered right. The professor's actions are creating a hostile environment. Even if the class laughed, that doesn't make it okay. The user's response was to call out the behavior, which is a form of self-advocacy. It's not aggressive in a violent way, just stating that it's not funny and using a hypothetical to show the other side.

However, some might argue that confronting the professor in class could be seen as disruptive, but the user's action was a direct response to the professor's behavior. The professor was the one initiating the inappropriate comments. The user's reaction was to address it directly, which is reasonable. The fact that the professor didn't respond and the class went quiet suggests that the comment was effective in stopping the behavior.

The kid who called him a dick might be part of the problem, but that's not the main issue. The main point is whether the user's action was morally acceptable. In most ethical frameworks, standing up against harassment is acceptable. Especially when the harassment is based on a protected characteristic like race, gender, or physical traits. Hair color isn't a protected characteristic in some places, but the principle of not being subjected to repeated derogatory comments still holds.

In a professional setting like a classroom, professors should maintain respect. Making jokes about a student's appearance repeatedly is unprofessional. So the student's response to call it out is justified. The way he did it was by stating it's not funny and using a counterexample, which is a reasonable way to point out the hypocrisy.

So morally acceptable. Answer should be 1.

Yes, I think 1 is correct. The action is morally acceptable.
